kjv: a cage of every unclean and hateful bird
mine: a haunt of every unclean bird, and a haunt of every unclean and hated beast
note: SBLGNT adds "kai phylakē pantos thēriou akathartou" (haunt of every unclean beast), which the TR lacks, so "hateful" attaches to the beasts rather than the birds.
SBLGNT reads peptōkan "have fallen"; the TR reads pepōken "has drunk". The two Greek words differ by one letter and the manuscripts are divided.

kjv: the wine of the wrath of her fornication
mine: the wine of the passion of her sexual immorality
note: Thymos can mean wrath or hot passion; here it most likely means the intoxicating passion of her immorality, though it may also hint at God's wrath (14:10).

mine: as she herself has paid out
note: The TR adds hymin "you" after apedōken; SBLGNT has no object, so the payback is not described as aimed at the hearers.
SBLGNT has the aorist ho krinas "who judged"; the TR has the present ho krinōn "who judges".
SBLGNT includes kai amōmon (amomum, an aromatic spice) after cinnamon; the TR omits it.

kjv: thou shalt find them no more
mine: people will never find them again
note: SBLGNT reads the third plural heurēsousin "they will find"; the TR has the second singular heurēsēs "you will find".
SBLGNT reads pas ho epi topon pleōn "everyone who sails to a place"; the TR reads pas epi tōn ploiōn ho homilos "all the company on the ships".

mine: you saints and apostles and prophets
note: SBLGNT reads hoi hagioi kai hoi apostoloi "the saints and the apostles", three groups called to rejoice; the TR reads hoi hagioi apostoloi "the holy apostles", making "holy" an adjective.
Lychnos is an oil lamp. "Candle" in 1611 meant any small light, but a modern reader pictures a wax candle.
